title: Grateful Dead Live at Robert F. Kennedy Stadium on 1973-06-09
lineage: AUDMR(Electro-Voice RE-15 super cardioid dynamic microphone > Nagra III Reel to Reel deck at 7.5 ips)  > DAT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Distant audience tape of the June 9 1973 RFK show captures a wildly psychedelic performance with standout They Love Each Other/Loose Lucy moments despite flat sound.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience source that sits back from the stage, giving a distant and somewhat flat sonic picture, but it still provides a unique listening angle. Musically the June 9 1973 RFK concert is remembered as one of the most "out there" shows, with mind‑blowing breaks on They Love Each Other/Loose Lucy and other memorable moments that have stuck with fans for decades.

ai_rating.rationale: Show is highly praised (multiple 5‑star reviews) while recording quality is noted as distant/flat, yielding a strong overall rating with high confidence due to several consistent reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Distant microphone placement makes the sound feel far back and somewhat flat; reviewers note occasional blemishes but appreciate the alternative perspective it offers.

show_quality.setlist_flow: An unpredictable, 'out there' set with surprising breaks that inject a mind‑blast into the music; fans recall unique improvisational moments and even a possible St. Stephen tease.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia is described as being in a parallel universe during song breaks, delivering otherworldly playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh similarly appears to be in a parallel universe, contributing powerful, psychedelic bass lines.
